edges.title: Split view pane, or the closed Duo turned left
edges.see: in column mode without children, the left 84px of the page is clipped, the controls draw over the content and an empty band runs down the right.
edges.cause: Safari's column is on the pane's left edge (or on the left when the closed Duo is turned to 90). Duet keeps the document scrolled one column across so the left column can paint, but the page content still starts at x 0, under the column.
edges.does: places the page itself: `margin-left` of the column width and the matching negative `margin-right` on `<html>`, marked `<html data-duet-reserve>`, with both insets 0. Centred content stays centred, nothing is clipped.
edges.you: nothing. Don't set `margin` on `<html>` or reset `scrollX`, Duet owns both. `<Duet reserve={false}>` opts out: the page runs under the column and `--duet-inset-left` / `--duet-inset-right` hold its width for `column()`, `bleed()` or your own padding.

edges.title: Rubber band at the top or bottom of the page
edges.see: in column mode without children, the controls leave their place as a group while the page bounces at either end (sliding up to 160pt over Safari's own column buttons, or out of the column), then come back once it settles.
edges.cause: the controls follow the document on a CSS scroll timeline, which is clamped to the scroll range. The iOS rubber band pushes `scrollY` past that range, and the in-document layer moves with the bounce.
edges.does: while the layer follows the document, `<html>` gets `overscroll-behavior-y: none`, so the document does not rubber-band, like a page with children. Only the Duo column is affected: other modes and other devices keep the bounce.
edges.you: nothing. The rule has zero specificity (`:where()`), so a page's own `overscroll-behavior` still wins, and with it the controls ride the bounce again.

edges.title: Toolbar growing back at the end of the page
edges.see: in column mode without children, after a flick to the end of the page the controls sit up to 18pt too high for about half a second, then snap back. Smaller 1 to 2pt jitters show while momentum scrolling.
edges.cause: the controls ride a CSS scroll timeline whose keyframe ends at the scroll range, `scrollHeight - innerHeight`. At the page end Safari's toolbar grows back after the scroll has stopped, sometimes seconds later, and `innerHeight` steps down (598, 586, 581, 580). Only `visualViewport` fires `resize` meanwhile, with no `scroll` and no window `resize` until it settles, so a range measured in JavaScript goes stale while the timeline's own range follows the live viewport.
edges.does: writes the range as `max(0px, <scrollHeight>px - 100dvh)`. `100dvh` follows `innerHeight` frame by frame, so CSS keeps the range live and JavaScript only reports `scrollHeight`. Measured on the simulator: a computed offset within 0.3pt of `scrollY` through the regrow (was 18pt), and 0.0pt during smooth `scrollIntoView` jumps.
edges.you: nothing. A fast flick toward the top can still paint a single frame (16ms) a few points off, from Safari's compositor sampling the scroll and the animation apart. If a page needs the controls perfectly still, pass `children` to `<Duet>`: the document then never scrolls, and the controls measure 0.0pt.

edges.title: Full-screen `position: fixed` overlay or modal backdrop
edges.see: without the handling, in column mode, while a modal or sheet scrim (`position: fixed; inset: 0`) is open, every Duet control in Safari's column disappears, the close button included, so the user has no way to close the sheet from the column.
edges.cause: Safari 26 hit-tests a point 4px in from the middle of each viewport edge for a fixed or sticky box and, when one covers it, paints that box's colour over the inset beyond that edge, Safari's column included, instead of the page's in-document content.
edges.does: on a Duo in Safari renders `.duet-guard`, a small invisible fixed box (16x64px, `pointer-events: none`, top `z-index`) on each viewport edge, so that hit test lands on it and the column keeps showing the controls. Your scrim stays `position: fixed`.
edges.you: nothing for a fixed `<div>` scrim. `<dialog>.showModal()` is not covered: its `::backdrop` sits in the top layer, above any `z-index`, so use a fixed `<div>` scrim instead. For one X, in the column, pass `close` to `<Duet>` while the sheet is open and hide the sheet's own X in column mode (`html[data-duet-mode="column"] .sheet-close { display: none; }`). See Modals and sheets in column mode.

edges.title: Page dialog open through a turn or fold
edges.see: without handling, with a full-screen page dialog open in a Safari tab on the closed Duo, turning the phone on its side and back upright leaves Safari's column without Duet's close button, and tapping where it was does nothing.
edges.cause: through the turn the page is in transit, not in column mode. A guard rendered only in column mode unmounts for those frames, Safari's edge hit test finds the scrim and fills the column with it, and that fill stays once the column and the guard are back.
edges.does: keeps `.duet-guard` mounted whenever the page is in Safari on a Duo, in every mode, so no frame of a turn, fold or unfold leaves the edge sample point on the scrim. The guard is invisible and takes no taps, so it changes nothing outside the column.
edges.you: nothing.

edges.title: Sideways swipe pans the page into the column
edges.see: a sideways swipe moves the whole page, controls included, into Safari's column, typically when a swipe runs off the end of a carousel or code block.
edges.cause: the controls widen the document by the column's width, so the document can scroll sideways, and `touch-action` on `<html>` stops at a horizontal scroller, whose overscroll chains to the document.
edges.does: sets `touch-action: pan-y` on `<html>` (and on the inner scroller with children), `overscroll-behavior-x: contain` on every element at zero specificity, and pins `scrollX` (0, or the column width for a left column) on every scroll, instantly, so a page's `scroll-behavior: smooth` can't turn it into a slow creep. Leaving the column resets `scrollX` to 0. Carousels and code blocks still scroll sideways.
edges.you: nothing. Your own `overscroll-behavior-x` wins over Duet's.

edges.title: Back/forward cache restore
edges.see: after going back to a page (`pageshow` with `persisted`), the controls start in the page and slide into the column over 2 to 3s, seen in a split left pane and on the closed Duo turned left.
edges.cause: a back/forward cache restore keeps the page's old state but not the old window, and the `scrollX` pin was a plain `scrollTo`, which a page's `html { scroll-behavior: smooth }` animated and each scroll event restarted.
edges.does: re-reads the signals on `pageshow`, re-pins `scrollX` with `behavior: "instant"`, and turns transitions off for 1.1s after a restore, as at first mount, so the controls land in place. Normal mode changes keep their ~250ms spring.
edges.you: nothing.

edges.title: In-app preview sheet
edges.see: a link opened from a social or mail app in the in-app Safari preview's page sheet got Safari-tab placement on a real Duo.
edges.cause: the sheet is a window inside the closed screen (450x670 on a real Duo), and its bottom safe-area inset reads 0 on the first sample and 34 about 100ms later, so the first reading looks like a tab.
edges.does: recognises a window inside the closed screen with the column signature and a bottom inset as the preview, and lets a tab verdict rise to preview during a window's first second. Turned sideways in the sheet, where the free gap is about 26pt, it hides the controls (`useDuet().hidden` is `"preview"`) so the preview's own buttons stay usable.
edges.you: nothing. Check `useDuet().preview` and `hidden` if your page lays out differently there.

edges.title: In-app preview filling the open screen
edges.see: a link opened in the in-app preview's default or full screen style on the unfolded Duo put the controls over the clock and Dynamic Island (wide) or on the preview's Page Menu (tall, turned right), and `useDuet().preview` read false.
edges.cause: these styles fill the open screen (951x669 or 669x951), unlike the sheet, so neither the closed nor the sheet signature matched. Wide, every native button sits in a 75pt top bar and the status column heads an 84pt inset on the right; tall turned right, the top bar floats over the page's first 54pt.
edges.does: recognises both windows by their chrome and inset (a tab has 126pt of bars and inset 34). Wide, it takes the right inset as a strip below the status column, with room for two Live Activities. Tall, it stays inline right and starts the controls below the top bar and the island.
edges.you: nothing.
edges.status: #108. Live Activities on the open screen are assumed to grow the island as on the closed one.

edges.title: Turning or folding mid-transition
edges.see: without the handling, the controls flash at the wrong edge during a turn, fold, unfold or split move, the page insets jump (up to 296px on a turn, -485px on an unfold), or Safari zooms the page to fit (scale 1.14).
edges.cause: there is no fold signal, and mid-transition the window passes through sizes no landed window has (inner and outer orientations disagree). The window size can land up to ~2s after the viewport, with no event. The column layer still carries the old posture's positions, which widen the document past the new window.
edges.does: keeps the last placement and hides the controls (`hidden` and `confidence` are `"moving"`) until the window lands and holds for 150ms (`LAND_HOLD`). The insets keep their last values, and the column layer is clipped out of the document width, so it adds no width until the landing. After each event it polls every 100ms until the sizes hold for 500ms, for at most 2s.
edges.you: nothing. If your own code reacts to `useDuet()`, ignore readings with `confidence: "moving"`.

edges.title: Unfolding the in-app preview
edges.see: without the handling, unfolding from the closed preview turned sideways leaves the closed screen's controls (the strip, or Safari's column) on the open screen for 50 to 130ms before they land inline.
edges.cause: WebKit holds `resize` back while the window animates, yet lays the page out every frame: the page took four sizes over ~220ms with no event. One of them, 585x876 in the 669x951 window, is the closed page's 84pt column handed the open window, which reads as Safari's column.
edges.does: also watches a viewport-sized box with a `ResizeObserver`, which reports every layout, so the window starts settling (controls hidden, `confidence: "moving"`) on the first new size. A column-wide page in the full open window is in transit, never the column: Safari has no column there.
edges.you: nothing.

edges.title: Text field focus and the on-screen keyboard
edges.see: without the handling, focusing an input in column mode makes Safari zoom out (to about 0.94), and the keyboard covers the lower column and the controls in it.
edges.cause: the column layer widens the document, and Safari zooms out to that width when a text field takes focus. The keyboard leaves Safari's column in place and only shrinks the visual viewport.
edges.does: from the moment a field (`:read-write:focus`, so inputs, textareas and `contenteditable`) takes focus, clips the column layer out of the document width and hides it, before the zoom and the keyboard. The keyboard never changes the mode. `useDuet().keyboard` is true while it is up, and `<Duet>` sets `data-keyboard`. In column mode the controls come back when focus leaves.
edges.you: nothing. Don't rely on Duet's column controls while the user types.

edges.title: Inline controls with the keyboard up
edges.see: without the handling, on the open screen in a Safari tab, the inline rail slides up as the keyboard rises: "…" goes off the top of the screen and the lower items end up under the keyboard.
edges.cause: iOS scrolls the layout viewport up by the keyboard's height (109pt on the open Duo) to keep the field in view, and a fixed rail moves with it.
edges.does: hides inline controls while `useDuet().keyboard` is true, as in column mode; they come back when the keyboard closes. Strip mode (Home Screen apps) is unchanged.
edges.you: nothing. Don't rely on Duet's inline controls while the user types.

edges.title: A short visual viewport after a turn, read as the keyboard
edges.see: without the handling, after turning the closed Duo from its side to upright (seen with a page dialog open), Duet's column controls stay hidden for good, as if the keyboard were up.
edges.cause: WebKit can leave `visualViewport.height` short after a turn (466 against a 580pt page) until the next resize, with no keyboard.
edges.does: counts the keyboard as up only while a text field (`:read-write`), a select or an iframe has focus, read through shadow roots, and re-reads on focus changes.
edges.you: nothing.

edges.title: Inline controls as the keyboard goes down
edges.see: without the handling, on the open screen in a Safari tab, tapping the page outside a focused field draws the inline rail about 107px too high for one frame, with "…" off the top of the screen, before it lands in place.
edges.cause: focus leaves first, while iOS still holds the layout viewport scrolled up by the keyboard (visual viewport 286 of 618). With no field focused that short viewport no longer counts as the keyboard (#122), so the rail showed at once.
edges.does: a keyboard that was up stays up after focus leaves until the visual viewport grows back, for at most 1s, so a viewport left short with no keyboard cannot hide the controls for good.
edges.you: nothing.

edges.title: Pinch zoom
edges.see: nothing changes while the page is zoomed: the mode and placement stay put.
edges.cause: with `visualViewport.scale` not 1, `innerWidth` is in zoomed px, so the window signature is unreadable.
edges.does: keeps the last context (`confidence: "held"`) until the scale returns to 1. Column mode also requires scale 1, so a page that loads zoomed starts `inline`.
edges.you: nothing.

edges.title: Safari's URL bar collapses
edges.see: `100vh` and `innerHeight` grow and shrink by 18px while the user scrolls, so full-screen sections jump.
edges.cause: Safari collapses its URL bar on scroll, which changes the page height.
edges.does: reports `useDuet().stableHeight`, the smallest page height seen at this window width and orientation, and sets it as `--duet-vh`. In column mode the page runs on under the floating URL bar, and `--duet-inset-bottom` reserves that space at the end of the scroller.
edges.you: size full-screen sections with `min-height: var(--duet-vh, 100svh)`.

edges.title: Live Activities and the top band
edges.see: an empty gap at the top of the strip or column, even when no Live Activity runs.
edges.cause: Live Activities grow the Dynamic Island down the strip and push Safari's buttons with it, and a page can't tell whether any are running.
edges.does: always reserves the worst case measured on device (two activities). `leading` and `primary` may rise into that space before they fold, back, actions and "…" never do. In the in-app preview nothing rises into it. Closed landscape was measured with a bare island only.
edges.you: nothing.

edges.title: Safari's forward button plus Live Activities
edges.see: without handling, Duet's buttons hide under Safari's in a closed tab once the page has forward history and two Live Activities run.
edges.cause: forward history grows Safari's back button into a 102.7pt back + forward pill, and the Live Activities push it down. The reader then ends at about 428 and the +/tabs pill starts at 541.6, so the band holds one button.
edges.does: puts "…" and the selected tab (or search) in one two-item rail, as tall as Safari's back + forward pill, centred between Safari's buttons and at least 5pt clear of each. Everything else folds into "…". Where even the rail has no room (closed landscape), the selected tab is the only button and its menu lists the tabs, then what folded. An island menu too wide for the screen opens as a morph instead.
edges.you: nothing. Keep the important actions first, they are the last to fold.

edges.title: In-app preview top bar compacting on scroll
edges.see: without handling, scrolling a page in the in-app preview (default or full style, closed portrait) moves Duet's controls out of the preview's column into an inline strip across the page.
edges.cause: the preview's top bar compacts as the page scrolls: the chrome above the page shrinks from 75 to 46px, below both the preview's old chrome range and the column's.
edges.does: takes 44 to 77px of chrome as the preview, and in the preview checks only the column's width, so it stays `column` with the controls in place through the scroll.
edges.you: nothing.

edges.title: In-app preview buttons and Live Activities
edges.see: without handling, a Live Activity pushes the preview's close and reader/menu buttons down onto Duet's controls in the gap.
edges.cause: Live Activities grow the Dynamic Island (one pushes those buttons about 45pt) while back stays put, and a page can't tell whether any are running.
edges.does: sizes the gap for the worst case (two activities, `DUO.island`), about 54pt: one button, the selected tab (or "…", or search), centred. Nothing rises into the space the activities can take, so no Duet button sits under a native one.
edges.you: nothing. Keep the important tabs and actions first, the tab's menu lists them.

edges.title: Shared with You bar
edges.see: without handling, a page opened from a link a contact sent in Messages loses the column: the controls drop into the page about a second after load while Safari's own column is still there.
edges.cause: Safari heads the page with a "From <name>" bar under the status bar until the user closes it. It adds 40pt to the top chrome (98 to 138 on the closed Duo, also in closed landscape and split panes), which fails the column check. Safari's column buttons don't move, the page starts 40pt lower.
edges.does: recognises the 40pt bar outside the full open window, keeps column mode and sets `useDuet().offsetTop` to 40, so every control lands where it does without the bar in screen points. `--duet-inset-bottom` stays the URL bar alone. Folding or splitting under the bar still reads as in transit.
edges.you: nothing. Unmeasured: the bar at the largest Dynamic Type, in the in-app preview and on scroll.

edges.title: In-app preview with forward history
edges.see: without handling, after going back once in the in-app preview, Duet's button covers the preview's Back.
edges.cause: with forward history the preview adds a Forward button where Back was and moves Back up a row (its top from 428 to 374pt), so the free gap ends higher.
edges.does: reads `navigation.canGoForward` (re-read on `currententrychange` and `popstate`) and, in the preview, ends the gap above the raised Back. That gap holds one button with no room left for Live Activities, so with forward history an activity may push the preview's reader/menu button onto Duet's button, never onto Back.
edges.you: nothing. The Navigation API only sees same-origin entries: coming back from another site, the preview shows Forward but Duet can't know, and its button may cover Back until the next same-origin navigation.

edges.title: Menus and popovers under Safari's buttons
edges.see: without the handling, a menu that reaches into the column is drawn under Safari's back, reader or +/tabs buttons.
edges.cause: Safari's native chrome always paints over the page, so `z-index` can't help.
edges.does: keeps its own menus between `columnTop` and Safari's pill, or opens them wholly over the page when they are too tall.
edges.you: keep your own popovers that cross the column below `--duet-safe-top-column` (0 outside column mode).

edges.title: Plain layout before mount
edges.see: on load, the page's column-mode styling (a band bled into the column, controls moved there) appears a moment after the plain layout, longer on a slow connection.
edges.cause: `data-duet-mode` and the `--duet-*` variables are set from an effect, after the first paint.
edges.does: ships `bootScript` (`duet-ui/boot`), which sets them before the first paint in column mode only.
edges.you: inline it at the top of `<body>`. See Pre-paint boot.

edges.title: Page modal turns off pointer events
edges.see: without the handling, the `close` passed to `<Duet>` shows in the column while a Radix or Headless UI sheet is open but does nothing.
edges.cause: those libraries set `pointer-events: none` on `<body>` while a modal is open, and the column layer inherits it.
edges.does: sets `pointer-events: auto` on `.duet`, like system chrome over the page.
edges.you: nothing.

edges.title: Column buttons fire on touch down
edges.see: buttons in Safari's column fire as the finger lands and show no native press state.
edges.cause: touches in the column reach the page but are not hit-tested to elements outside the viewport, and Safari usually keeps the touch end.
edges.does: listens for `pointerdown`, finds the button under the touch's coordinates and clicks it. In a split pane, the tap also tells Duet which side the pane is on.
edges.you: nothing. Don't put anything that needs a long press or a drag in the column.

edges.title: Animations removed by a page reset
edges.see: in column mode without children, the controls lag behind momentum scroll.
edges.cause: a reset like `* { animation: none !important }` (common under reduced motion) removes the scroll timeline the layer follows the document on, and so does a browser without scroll-timeline support.
edges.does: falls back to a transform set on every scroll event, which lags in momentum.
edges.you: exclude `.duet` from the reset, or pass the page as `children` (the steadier choice in any case).

edges.title: Tab labels while scrubbing
edges.see: without the handling, holding and dragging on the tab pill shows every label except the one under your finger.
edges.cause: the real tabs are cut away under the lens, so only its magnified copy shows there, and that copy had icons only.
edges.does: draws the labels in the lens copy too, magnified with the icon.
edges.you: keep labels short (about 10 characters); longer ones are clipped to the tab's width. Where they matter, `minimizeOnScroll="always"` with `menuStyle="morph"` lists them in full.

edges.title: Viewport meta and `viewport-fit=cover`
edges.see: without the handling, Safari zooms a split pane out to fit the widened document, and `strip` mode is never detected.
edges.cause: Safari shrinks the page to fit wide content unless the viewport meta says `shrink-to-fit=no`, and safe-area insets only reach the page with `viewport-fit=cover`. Frameworks add and rewrite viewport metas after load.
edges.does: appends `shrink-to-fit=no` on import and `viewport-fit=cover` when `<Duet>` mounts, to every viewport meta, and keeps them on metas added or rewritten later. With no viewport meta it adds `width=device-width,initial-scale=1` first.
edges.you: nothing, but don't set `viewport-fit=contain` or `shrink-to-fit=yes`: Duet only appends absent keys and leaves your values as they are.

edges.title: Mode flips back and forth
edges.see: without the handling, the controls jump between the column and the page several times a second.
edges.cause: column mode can feed back into the signals, for example when Safari zooms the page out to fit the wider document, the column signature disappears, `inline` removes the overflow, and the signature returns.
edges.does: after 3 mode changes within 2s at the same window size, pauses column mode for 3s, doubling each time the loop resumes right after the pause, up to 60s. Changes while the window is still settling are not counted.
edges.you: nothing.

edges.title: Mode detection limits
edges.see: `inline` where you expected the column or the strip, or a Duo layout on a device that is not a Duo.
edges.cause: iOS gives a web page no API for the device, the fold or Safari's buttons. Duet infers everything from window and screen sizes measured on the Duo, safe-area insets, display mode and the user agent.
edges.does: uses the column only in Safari (not Chrome, Firefox, Edge or other apps' browsers), never in an iframe, and gives in-app web views (a user agent without `Safari/`) `inline`. A Duo whose reported sizes differ (display zoom, a future iOS release) gets `inline`, and an iPad or another device with matching sizes may read as a Duo.
edges.you: use `useDuet().duo` to switch to a Duo layout, not as proof of the device. Check `useDuet().browser` to tell why a page is `inline`. For server-rendered layouts, see Server rendering.
edges.status: 0.2.2. See Is this an iPhone Duo? and Which mode.

edges.title: Call to action in a closed Safari tab
edges.see: without the handling, a page's main action (Book, Buy) folds into "…" on the closed Duo, while the tabs keep the slot by the thumb.
edges.cause: in a closed tab Safari's own buttons leave the band room for two controls, and "…" always takes one.
edges.does: with `primary.prominent`, gives the thumb slot to the call to action and folds the tabs (or search) into "…" as a radio group at the top of the menu. With forward history and Live Activities, "…" and the call to action share the two-item rail, the call to action as a tinted bubble.
edges.you: mark only the page's one main action `prominent`, and keep tabs reachable another way on that page if they matter (back, or the "…" menu).

edges.title: Call to action opens over the page
edges.see: a call to action that loads as a wide labelled pill reads as an open card over the content, before the user has done anything.
edges.cause: the pill grows toward the page to fit its label, so on load it covers part of the page.
edges.does: starts a prominent primary closed, as the tinted round button, and opens it into the pill only with `expanded: true`, on the same spring as label changes.
edges.you: leave it closed by default; set `expanded` for a state worth reading (Booking, Booked), or from the start on a page whose whole point is the action.
